title: Eval & Quality Monitoring Demo - NovaHealth
header: Date: 2025-03-04 | Start: 14:00 PST | Duration: 42 mins | Attendees: Sam Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Rao (Redwood SE), Luis Gomez (Redwood CSM), Emma Lin (NovaHealth CPO), Marco Silva (NovaHealth Lead ML Eng), Janelle Park (NovaHealth Data Ops), Aaron Wu (NovaHealth Security)
summary: Redwood demo of Eval / Quality Monitoring (Console + API + Optimize). Covered prompt set management, regression alerts, A/B comparison workflows, and integration points for NovaHealth's private deployment. Customer focused on regression detection thresholds, data residency, and pilot success criteria. Agreed next steps: share benchmark spreadsheet, security docs, and schedule pilot kickoff + baseline eval run.
topics: API endpoints for evals and datasets
action_items: Sam Chen - Share pricing sheet and pilot agreement - due 2025-03-07
Priya Rao - Send benchmark spreadsheet and example prompt set CSV - due 2025-03-06
Janelle Park - Provide sample prompt sets and top 200 examples from prod - due 2025-03-05
Aaron Wu - Confirm required compliance docs (SOC2 scope, encryption key policy) - due 2025-03-10
next_steps: Redwood to run baseline eval on NovaHealth sample prompts (1k prompts) and share results
Sam to send security pack + SOC2 report link
Schedule 60-min pilot kickoff the week of 2025-03-10
Customer to confirm pilot stakeholders and SLAs to validate
transcript:
[00:00] Sam Chen: hey everyone thanks for joining, uh we'll get started in a minute, hope that's okay. 
[00:08] Emma Lin: yeah great, thanks Sam. we've been excited to see how you do evals at Redwood, we run models across a couple of providers and want tighter quality monitoring. 
[00:16] Priya Rao: awesome, i'll jump in with a live demo of the console and the optimize recommendations, and then show the API flow for running prompt sets and registering regression alerts. 
[00:30] Marco Silva: quick FYI, our main concerns are false positives on regressions and model drift, and then the latency/cost tradeoff for doing continuous evals. 
[00:38] Priya Rao: totally. so high level: Redwood's Eval/Quality Monitoring ties prompt sets, automated metrics, and alerts together. you can run A/B comparisons, compare model variants, and set thresholds on metrics like exact match, rouge, and custom scoring. 
[00:50] Sam Chen: we'll also cover how Optimize suggests batching/quant profiles to reduce per-token cost while keeping the same eval pass rate. 
[01:00] Luis Gomez: quick note i'll record action items here and share the recording. 
[01:05] Janelle Park: sounds good. can you show how we import our existing prompt set? we have CSVs exported from our internal tool. 
[01:12] Priya Rao: yep, show you both the Console UI and the API. in the console you go to Eval -> Prompt Sets -> Import CSV, map columns, then you can attach expected responses or scoring functions. i'll do that now. 
[01:28] [screen share noise] Priya Rao: okay i'm dragging in a sample CSV, mapping prompt_text to prompt and expected to expected_answer, now it's uploaded, note that the import can detect duplicate prompts and flag near-duplicates with fuzzy matching (sometimes it's a bit aggressive depending on typos). 
[01:45] Emma Lin: that's useful — we have a lot of paraphrases. how are the alert thresholds configured? we want to avoid daily noise. 
[01:52] Priya Rao: you can set rolling window thresholds, e.g. 7-day average drop of 2% in exact match triggers a warning, 5% triggers a page. and you can tie alerts to channels (email, slack, webhook). plus you can set sampling rules so only a subset of traffic runs the eval to control cost. 
[02:10] Marco Silva: can we run A/B where variant A is our tuned raven-13b and variant B is the new open-13b quantized? also will KV cache or context length affect eval comparability? 
[02:20] Priya Rao: yes you can compare any two model endpoints; the system normalizes by inference recipe, though you should pin sequence length and sampling parameters. KV cache doesn't affect outputs for evaluation if you're sending isolated prompts, but for stateful sessions you can snapshot KV state. 
[02:35] Aaron Wu: security question — will eval data leave our VPC? we need to ensure PHI doesn't go to hosted endpoints. 
[02:42] Sam Chen: good question. for NovaHealth we discussed Private deployment — Redwood Private keeps inference inside your VPC and we can use your KMS/HSM for keys. logs can be forwarded to your SIEM, we also support audit-log retention policies. 
[02:58] Aaron Wu: okay please send the SOC2 scope and details on key management. 
[03:05] Priya Rao: noted, i'll attach the SOC2 report and KMS integration doc. 
[03:10] [00:03:10] Priya Rao: back to demo, i'll create a regression alert. clicking Alerts -> New Alert -> name it 'NOVA health exact match drop' -> metric exact_match -> baseline is last 30 days -> threshold -3% -> severity warning. you can see the UI shows recent trend lines and examples that failed, and it's linked to the prompt set so you can inspect failing prompts and the model outputs side-by-side. 
[03:40] Emma Lin: can we customize scoring? we have a domain-specific rubric with weighted criteria. 
[03:46] Priya Rao: yes, the console supports custom scoring hooks — you can upload a function (JS or Python snippet) or call a webhook to run scoring; the evaluation pipeline supports per-prompt metadata and per-criterion weights. caveat: if you run scoring via webhook there's additional latency. 
[04:05] Marco Silva: what about A/B analysis statistics, do you do statistical significance testing? 
[04:12] Priya Rao: we do bootstrap confidence intervals and an A/B summary table. the console flags statistically significant differences after X samples; you can set X or use the default 1k samples for better power. 
[04:25] Emma Lin: great. how do you handle reranking or multi-step prompts? our flows sometimes do generate->rerank->finalize. 
[04:33] Priya Rao: you can define multi-step evals that execute the pipeline and evaluate at each step, or you can record intermediate outputs and run custom aggregations. the API supports passing an array of messages for multi-turn. 
[04:50] Sam Chen: just to echo the cost note — continuous full eval on all traffic is expensive; Optimize can recommend sampling rates and batching to hit a budget target. 
[04:58] Marco Silva: show me the optimize suggestions. 
[05:02] Priya Rao: heading to Redwood Optimize -> Recommendations. for a given workload it suggests quantization level, per-model batching, and KV cache settings. for example for open-13b it suggests int8 q4f16 and batch size 8 for your latency SLO of ~300ms, which reduces token cost ~30% in our sim. 
[05:25] Janelle Park: handy. is there a way to preview the eval results in bulk? we want CSV exports for downstream dashboards. 
[05:32] Priya Rao: yes export as CSV or JSON; we also offer a webhook sink to push eval results into your data lake. note sometimes the webhook delivery can retry and duplicate if not idempotent. 
[05:45] [crosstalk] Emma Lin: do you have any case studies with health care customers? 
[05:51] Sam Chen: we have an anonymized case study and a benchmark spreadsheet; i'll share both links. 
[05:58] [08:00] Priya Rao: jumping ahead to API, here's the eval run endpoint: POST /v1/evals/run with body {prompt_set_id, model_variant, sampling_rule}. you can programmatically create prompt sets, run batches, and subscribe to alerts. note: some transcribers show curly braces oddly, ignore that. 
[06:25] Marco Silva: will the API return per-prompt diffs? we want unified diffs for the A/B comparison. 
[06:30] Priya Rao: yes the API returns per-prompt outputs for each variant and a diff summary object with metric deltas and confidence intervals. small caveat: very long outputs may be truncated in the UI but full outputs are in the export. 
[06:48] Emma Lin: i want to understand false positives — will you surface every single minor drop? 
[06:53] Priya Rao: by default no, alerts are configurable with severity and rolling windows; plus you can mark certain prompt groups as 'do not trigger' or tune the alert to only fire when both metric drop and increase in failed-case ratio happen. 
[07:08] Janelle Park: ok what about drift detection over time? 
[07:12] Priya Rao: we have drift detectors that track embedding-space shifts and distributional changes; when drift crosses a threshold it can trigger a re-eval or a manual review task. embeddings are computed via Redwood's embed API or you can provide your own. 
[07:28] Marco Silva: how does this integrate with our CI? can we gate model rollouts on eval gates? 
[07:33] Priya Rao: yes you can add eval gates in your CI workflow using the API. if the eval fails the rollout can be blocked or auto-rolled back depending on policy. 
[07:45] Aaron Wu: also need proof of data handling, retention. we can't keep PHI past 30 days for eval traces. 
[07:52] Sam Chen: we can set retention per-customer and per-route; for Private deployments retention happens in your infra. we'll share the retention config doc. 
[08:00] Priya Rao: quick demo of A/B results table — shows overall metrics, per-prompt fails, and example diffs. i'll flag an example where variant B has higher fluency but lower domain accuracy. 
[08:18] Emma Lin: do you support human-in-the-loop re-labeling or quick triage? 
[08:23] Priya Rao: yes, you can create review queues and assign to annotators; there's an approval workflow to accept new golden answers into the prompt set. 
[08:35] Marco Silva: for the pilot we'd want to run 1k prompts, compare our tuned model against upstream open-13b quantized, and set alert thresholds to only surface >3% drop. 
[08:45] Sam Chen: that's doable. action items captured. 
[09:00] [09:00] Priya Rao: last piece: latency-aware sampling. you can sample more for low latency routes and less for high-latency expensive calls. Optimize will simulate cost/latency tradeoffs for you. 
[09:18] Janelle Park: one more question — will the eval pipeline preserve PII redaction? we sometimes need redaction. 
[09:25] Priya Rao: we offer built-in redaction hooks and you can run pre-processing lambdas to remove or tokenise PII before eval. again for Private we recommend processing inside VPC. 
[09:40] Aaron Wu: please include the architecture diagram that shows data flows for private evals. 
[09:45] Sam Chen: will do. 
[09:48] Emma Lin: ok i'm comfortable moving to pilot if we see the security pack and baseline results. 
[09:54] Sam Chen: great — we'll run baseline and share results. 
[10:00] [10:00] Priya Rao: quick note — sometimes the auto-transcript mislabels product names like Redwood Opti-mise or redwood console with lower-case, apologies for the messy transcript. 
[10:10] Marco Silva: ha, no worries. 
[10:15] Sam Chen: any final Qs? 
[10:18] Janelle Park: none from me. Marco? 
[10:20] Marco Silva: all good. 
[10:22] Emma Lin: thanks everyone. 
[10:24] Sam Chen: thanks, we'll follow up with the docs and scheduling. recap: Sam to send pricing + security pack; Priya to send benchmark csv and run baseline eval; Janelle to provide sample prompts. 
[10:40] [END]
